items.definition: how to compare two or more things when you shop
items.explanationTR:
When we compare two things, we use the comparative form of an adjective. For short adjectives (one syllable), add -er: cheap becomes cheaper, small becomes smaller. If the adjective ends in a consonant plus -y, change y to i and add -er: easy becomes easier. If it ends in one vowel plus one consonant, double the last letter: big becomes bigger, hot becomes hotter. For longer adjectives (two or more syllables), use more plus the adjective: expensive becomes more expensive, comfortable becomes more comfortable.

When we compare three or more things, we use the superlative form. Add -est for short adjectives, with the word the in front: cheap becomes the cheapest, small becomes the smallest. For longer adjectives, use the most plus the adjective.

• This store is cheaper than that one.
• These shoes are more comfortable than my old ones.
• This is the best shop in the mall.
• That was the most expensive jacket I've ever bought.
• Prices here are lower than online.

A few adjectives are irregular: good becomes better, then the best; bad becomes worse, then the worst. Remember to use than after a comparative (cheaper than) and the before a superlative (the cheapest).

questions.prompt: These jeans are ---- than the ones in the other store.
questions.explanationTR: Cheap is a one-syllable adjective, so the comparative form adds -er: cheaper. "More cheap" is not correct, and "cheapest"/"the cheapest" are superlative forms for three or more things, not for a comparison between two.

questions.prompt: This is ---- store in the whole mall.
questions.explanationTR: With three or more things (the whole mall), we need the superlative: the biggest. "Bigger" is a comparative, used with than for two things, and "more big" is not correct.

questions.prompt: The leather wallet is ---- than the plastic one.
questions.explanationTR: Expensive has three syllables, so its comparative form is more expensive, not expensiver. The superlative forms (most expensive, the most expensive) are used to compare three or more things.

questions.prompt: Of all the shops downtown, this one is ---- .
questions.explanationTR: "Of all the shops" compares more than two things, so we need the superlative with "the": the most popular. "More popular" is a comparative form, used for comparing two things with than.

questions.prompt: The service at this store is ---- than at the last one.
questions.explanationTR: Good is irregular: its comparative form is better, not gooder or more good. "Best"/"the best" are superlative forms, used for three or more things.

questions.prompt: That was ---- sale I've ever seen - nothing was really cheap.
questions.explanationTR: Bad is irregular, and its superlative form is the worst, not baddest or more bad. "Worse" is the comparative form, used to compare two things.

options: This shirt is more nicer than that one.
This shirt is nicer than that one.
This shirt is most nice than that one.
This shirt is nicer as that one.
This shirt is the nicer than that one.
questions.explanationTR: Nice is a short adjective, so its comparative form is simply nicer, followed by than. We never double the comparative with more, and we don't use as or the with a comparative plus than.

questions.prompt: Finding a parking spot here is ---- than at the big mall.
questions.explanationTR: Easy ends in a consonant plus y, so the comparative form changes y to i and adds -er: easier. "Easyer" is a spelling mistake, and "more easy" is not correct for a short adjective.

items.definition: A short article about smart shopping habits, with seven questions

passage.title: Smart Shopping Tips
passage.body:
Shopping can be fun, but it is easy to spend too much money. Here are some simple tips for smart shopping.

First, always make a shopping list before you go to the store. A list helps you buy only the things you really need. Second, compare prices before you buy something expensive, like a phone or a jacket. The same product can be cheaper in a different store or online.

Third, look for sales and discounts, but don't buy something just because it's on sale. Ask yourself: do I really need this? A cheap item is not a bargain if you never use it.

Fourth, keep your receipts. If something breaks or doesn't fit, you can return it or ask for a refund. Most stores will help you if you have the receipt.

Finally, make a budget before you go shopping and try to stay within it. It is easy to spend more than you planned, especially at a big mall with hundreds of stores.

If you follow these tips, you can save money and still buy the things you need.

questions.prompt: What should you do before you go to the store, according to the text?
options: Ask a friend to come with you
questions.explanationTR: The text says to always make a shopping list before you go to the store, so you buy only what you need. The other options are not mentioned in the text.

questions.prompt: Why does the text say it is a good idea to compare prices?
options: Because stores always have the same price
Because the same product can be cheaper somewhere else
Because comparing prices is required by law
Because online stores never have sales
questions.explanationTR: The text explains that the same product can be cheaper in a different store or online, so comparing prices can save you money. The other options contradict the text.

questions.prompt: According to the text, when is a cheap item not really a bargain?
options: When it is in a big mall
When the store gives a discount
questions.explanationTR: The text says a cheap item is not a bargain if you never use it. Being on sale or having a discount does not make something a good buy on its own.

questions.prompt: Why should you keep your receipts, according to the text?
options: To get a discount next time
To return an item or get a refund
questions.explanationTR: The text says that if something breaks or doesn't fit, you can return it or ask for a refund if you have the receipt. The other options are not what the text says receipts are for.

questions.prompt: What does the text say about your budget?
options: Spend all of it at the mall
Make it after you go shopping
questions.explanationTR: The text says to make a budget before you go shopping and try to stay within it. "Make it after you go shopping" is wrong because the text says to make it before.

questions.prompt: What does the text say about big malls?
options: It's easy to spend more than planned there
They are cheaper than small stores
questions.explanationTR: The text warns that it is easy to spend more than you planned, especially at a big mall with hundreds of stores. The other statements are not supported by the text.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Simple habits can help you shop smart and save money
You should always buy the cheapest item
Sales are always a bad idea
You should never use a credit card
questions.explanationTR: The text gives several simple tips, like making a list and comparing prices, that together help you shop smart and save money. The other options are too extreme and not what the text says.
